---
title: "<<- creates a global variable when it finds nothing to modify"
ref: FUN-08
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "a variable local to the function, or an error"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
count_values <- function(x) {
  n_values <<- length(x)
  n_values
}
exists("n_values")
count_values(1:3)
exists("n_values")
n_values
```
:::

## Why

`<<-` does not create the variable inside the function: it walks up the parent environments looking for a variable with that name, in order to modify it. If it finds none, it creates it in the global environment.

The function then leaves a trace in the workspace. Worse, if a variable `n_values` already existed, it is overwritten without warning.

## The remedy

Return the value and assign it at the call site. Keep `<<-` for closures, where the variable already exists in the enclosing function.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
count_values <- function(x) {
  length(x)
}
n <- count_values(1:3)
n
```
:::
